category_title: Third-grade African American students who rely on picture support and skip text when overwhelmed
student_description: Tommy is a confident reader who becomes overwhelmed by high word density, leading him to skip text and over-rely on picture clues. He often makes meaning-changing miscues based on illustrations but believes he is using effective reading strategies. He uniquely needs his visual strategies validated before being redirected to explicit text chunking, as well as audio playback of his reading to help him independently recognize his errors.

criteria.rationale: Because Tommy believes guessing from pictures is an effective reading strategy, acknowledging this effort prevents him from feeling shut down before he is redirected.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly acknowledges or validates the student's use of the illustration before prompting him to look at the text.

criteria.rationale: Tommy becomes overwhelmed by word density and defaults to skipping or guessing, so he needs immediate, explicit support to break words down into manageable pieces.
criteria.check: The tutor directs the student's attention back to the letters of the specific word and guides them to break it into smaller, decodable parts.
